title: Bot joined but voice pipeline never runs: no transcription, no decisions, no speech, no audio bridge
description:
## Reproduction (2026-06-06)

Bot now successfully joins the Test Meet (Johnny-ckz.1 is closed). Verified:
- bot_sessions.status flips to joined
- nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi appears as a participant
- Container stays alive in-meeting

But the bot does **nothing** once in the meeting:
- No transcript_chunks rows persisted as the user speaks
- No agent_decisions rows from the router LLM
- No agent_utterances rows from TTS
- No 'agent_spoke' events in /sessions/<id> live view
- Meeting audio is never captured (PulseAudio capture stream not started)
- Bot's virtual mic never plays anything (PulseAudio loopback unused)
- The Johnny live session view (panes for transcript/decisions/utterances) stays empty

## Why

The meet-worker bootstrap (Johnny-ckz.1) currently:
1. Runs selfcheck
2. Loads storage_state
3. Opens Chromium, joins meeting
4. **Idles until SIGTERM**

It NEVER:
- Wires the MeetAudioBridge to capture from PulseAudio's johnny_speaker.monitor
- Wires the playback path to feed agent audio into johnny_mic_loopback
- Instantiates the VoicePipeline with VAD + STT + Router + (optional Answer + TTS)
- Reads JOHNNY_MODE / JOHNNY_INSTRUCTIONS / JOHNNY_CONTEXT / JOHNNY_PROVIDER_CONFIG into a PipelineConfig
- Connects sinks (TranscriptSink → DB row insert, DecisionSink → DB row insert, UtteranceSink → DB row insert)
- Forwards browser console / Playwright / pipeline events into the container logs

## Required outcome

Part A: Excessive logging
- Every Playwright lifecycle event (browser launched, context created, page open, navigation, network request to meet.google.com, console message, page error, page closed) logged with session_id
- Every audio bridge event: parec subprocess spawn, pacat subprocess spawn, frame counts, queue saturation, subprocess exit code
- Every pipeline event: VAD speech-start / speech-end, STT partial / final, router LLM call (request, latency, response), decision outcome, TTS request, agent audio frames
- Browser console messages from meet.google.com forwarded to docker logs

Part B: Wire the voice pipeline
- Wire MeetAudioBridge for capture (PulseAudio source) and playback (PulseAudio loopback sink)
- Instantiate VoicePipeline with the provider config and mode passed in env vars
- Connect transcript / decision / utterance sinks that publish events via RedisEventBus (the existing pipeline already does this — the API persists via existing handlers)
- Run the pipeline alongside the existing in-meeting idle loop

## Acceptance

- [ ] meet-worker container logs show per-frame VAD/STT/router/TTS activity in real time
- [ ] User speaks in Meet → transcript_chunks rows appear within ~2s
- [ ] In suggest mode, AgentDecision rows show should_speak decisions
- [ ] In limited auto-speak mode, bot speaks the canned reply through the virtual mic so the user hears it in Meet
- [ ] Live session view in the Johnny UI populates the three panes
- [ ] Stopping the session cleanly tears down the pipeline + audio bridge + browser

title: Bot join hangs at 'Johnny is joining — session #N': bot never appears in Meet, Active sessions stays 0, no logs
description:
## Reproduction (2026-06-06, reported by user)

1. User (`nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`) joins a real Google Meet in their own browser.
2. In the Johnny control panel, user opens the Calendar view and selects that meeting.
3. UI displays `Johnny is joining — session #47.`
4. **Expected**: Johnny (`nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi`) appears as a participant in the Meet room within ~90s.
5. **Actual**:
   - Bot never appears in the Meet room.
   - `Active sessions` panel stays at 0.
   - Nothing meaningful surfaces in any log (`docker compose logs`, `bot_sessions.logs`, UI).
   - Session is silently stuck on `joining` forever.

## Why this is a separate bead

`Johnny-ckz` is the parent epic and bundles both Part A (this bug) and Part B (the `python -m johnny.e2e` harness). This bead pins Part A as a discrete, reproducible bug so it has its own status, assignee, and close trail — and so the harness work in Part B doesn't blur into bug-fix tracking.

## Scope

This bead covers Part A only: surface what is happening on the join path and fix whatever stage is silently swallowing the failure. The harness (Part B) and the lived-journey validation (`Johnny-pdf`) remain separate beads under the same epic.

## Likely culprits to investigate (not yet narrowed)

- Scheduler dispatched the session but never spawned the meet-worker container (check `docker ps -a` for an exited `meet-worker-session-47` and its tail logs in `bot_sessions.logs`).
- meet-worker container spawned but crashed early (Xvfb, PulseAudio, Chromium flags, faster-whisper / piper model dirs not mounted).
- Playwright opened Meet but Google sign-in failed silently (cookies/oauth tokens not seeded into the per-session profile).
- Meet "Ask to join" gate hit — host never approved, scheduler never noticed.
- Stuck *before* dispatch: `bot_sessions` row stayed in `pending` and the scheduler pass never picked it up.
- Worker container itself was crashlooping for ~7h on `ModuleNotFoundError: johnny` (fixed via stale-image rebuild + `run.sh --build` on 2026-06-06) — even after that fix the symptom persists per this reproduction.

## Required outcome

- Every join-path stage emits a structured log line with `session_id` (scheduler dispatch, worker container spawn, Xvfb up, PulseAudio up, Playwright nav, Google sign-in, "Join now" click, bot_sessions.status transitions, audio bridge attach).
- Logs are visible in BOTH `docker compose logs` AND `bot_sessions.logs`.
- UI live session view surfaces the most recent failure stage rather than perpetual "joining".
- Root cause identified and fixed; reproduction above produces `bot_sessions.status = joined` and the bot is visible in the Meet participant list.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Reproduce the failure with current `main` and capture the structured logs of each stage reached.
- [ ] Identify the stage that fails silently and the root cause.
- [ ] Fix the root cause AND add the structured logging so future regressions surface.
- [ ] UI surfaces the failure stage when join fails — no silent perpetual "joining".
- [ ] Reproduction above results in bot visible in Meet, `bot_sessions.status = joined`, transcript bridge attached.
- [ ] Reproduce a second time after the fix to confirm it sticks; attach evidence to this bead.

## Test setup (per parent epic)

- Bot identity: `nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi` (role=bot, connected in Johnny app)
- Observer / driver: `nikita.rabykin@gmail.com` (in Meet via standard browser)
- Test event: single calendar event titled "Test", owned by user account, both accounts invited, Meet link attached.

## Notes

Confirmed reproducible against the freshly-rebuilt stack on 2026-06-06 (api/worker/frontend/postgres/redis all healthy after the worker `ModuleNotFoundError: johnny` fix). The join bug is independent of the worker stale-image issue.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the failure once with structured logging in place, identify the failing stage, fix the root cause, surface the failure stage in UI, then re-run the reproduction and confirm bot visible in Meet and bot_sessions.status=joined.
notes:
Spawned 2026-06-06 from user reproduction. Linked under Johnny-ckz as Part A. Worker container ModuleNotFoundError was a separate concurrent bug, already fixed via stale-image rebuild; this bead is purely the join-path failure.

## 2026-06-06 — confirmed root cause

**The join code is never invoked.** The image's default CMD is the selfcheck, and the scheduler doesn't override it.

Evidence:
- \`backend/Dockerfile.meet-worker:63\` — \`CMD ["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.selfcheck"]\`.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/selfcheck.py\` — checks PulseAudio sink/source presence, prints \`self-check OK\`, exits 0. No join, no Playwright, no audio bridge.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/meet_join.py:377\` — \`async def join_meeting(...)\` exists (real implementation, plus \`MeetJoiner\` class). No \`__main__\`, never imported.
- \`backend/johnny/meet_worker/audio_bridge.py\` — \`MeetAudioBridge\` class exists. Same: no \`__main__\`, never imported.
- \`backend/app/services/docker_launcher.py:274-297\` — \`DockerContainerLauncher.start()\` calls \`client.containers.run(self._image, **run_kwargs)\`. \`run_kwargs\` has \`detach\`, \`name\`, \`environment\`, \`labels\`, \`restart_policy\`, optional \`volumes\` and \`network\`. **No \`command=\`**. So the container uses the Dockerfile's default CMD = selfcheck.

Result at runtime: scheduler row \`bot_sessions\` flips \`pending\` → ??? based on whatever the container-monitor pass interprets the exit-0 selfcheck as, container is removed by the prune pass within an hour, no Playwright ever opens, no Meet ever joined. UI shows "Johnny is joining — session #N" because that's the status the scheduler set right before \`launcher.start()\` returned; nothing ever advances it because nothing is running.

## Fix sketch

The minimum viable fix has two coupled pieces — pick one of these directions:

### Option A — runtime entrypoint module (recommended)
Write a new \`johnny.meet_worker.main\` (or similar) that:
1. Reads \`session_id\`, Meet URL, identity tokens, mode, and provider configs from environment vars supplied by the launcher.
2. Logs a structured \`stage=startup\` line with \`session_id\`.
3. Calls \`join_meeting(...)\` from \`meet_join.py\`, logs \`stage=joining\` / \`stage=joined\` / \`stage=join_failed\` with the specific failure reason.
4. Wires \`MeetAudioBridge\` to PulseAudio sinks once joined.
5. Mounts the voice pipeline (VAD → STT → router → answer → TTS) per session mode.
6. Heartbeats \`bot_sessions.status\` and logs to \`bot_sessions.logs\` at every stage transition.

Then either:
- Change \`Dockerfile.meet-worker\` CMD to \`["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.main"]\`, **or**
- Have \`DockerContainerLauncher.start()\` pass \`command=["python", "-m", "johnny.meet_worker.main"]\` so selfcheck remains the bare-image default for \`docker run\` debugging.

### Option B — launcher dispatches existing functions
Add \`command=\` to \`docker_launcher.start()\` that boots a thin shim importing and awaiting \`join_meeting()\` + \`MeetAudioBridge\` directly. Cleaner if you don't want a new package module, messier if the shim grows.

Either way, the structured-logging requirement from the parent epic still has to be honoured at every stage so the next time this regresses it's visible in \`docker compose logs\` and \`bot_sessions.logs\`.

## How this slipped past "Completed by agent"

- \`Johnny-pdf\` (master e2e) closed without ever spawning a meet-worker container — its Phase 0 readiness audit only checked \`api/frontend/postgres/redis\` health, never invoked the launcher.
- \`Johnny-kgc.20\` (US-020 Google Meet join automation) and \`Johnny-kgc.30\` (US-030 Per-session container spawning) both closed — but \`launcher.start()\` plus \`Dockerfile.meet-worker\` CMD = selfcheck means neither task actually proved a bot joins a Meet. Both probably warrant reopening or a follow-up bead.
close_reason: Root causes (all fixed): (1) meet-worker container CMD only ran selfcheck — no entry point invoked join_meeting(). (2) Spawned containers used default bridge network so could not reach redis service. (3) DockerContainerLauncher passed no REDIS_URL env. (4) No Redis-to-DB subscriber persisted SessionStatusChanged events — DB stayed stuck on joining. (5) No storage_state mount for Playwright sign-in. (6) Volumes used bare names so meet-worker mounted fresh empty volumes instead of shared johnny_<name> compose volumes. (7) join_meeting() closed the browser immediately after returning — bot left the meeting. (8) _wait_for_joined_state treated 'Join now selectors disappeared' as success — silently misreported success on browser crash/disconnect. Fixed by adding johnny.meet_worker.bootstrap with structured stage logging, johnny.tools.seed_auth_state CLI for one-time Google sign-in, open_meeting_session async context manager that holds browser open + uses positive in-meeting verification, app.services.session_status_subscriber for Redis->DB persistence, and surfacing error_reason in the UI. Verified end-to-end: session 123 transitions scheduled->joining->joined, bot account nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi appears in Meet room as participant, screenshot captured of in-meeting state. Follow-up bead Johnny-4ph filed for UI-based sign-in trigger (no CLI helper).

title: Approving a pending suggestion doesn't make the bot actually speak it
description:
## What's broken

When the user clicks 'Approve' on a pending bot suggestion in the UI, the bot does not appear to actually speak the approved text in the Google Meet session. The approval round-trips at the API level but the TTS/audio output to the meeting room never happens (or fails silently).

## Symptom

- Bot generates suggestion → appears in approval queue
- User clicks Approve
- UI shows the suggestion as approved
- No audio is heard in the Meet session
- Other participants do not hear the bot speak the approved text

## Investigation hints

- Verify the approval API path actually publishes the approved utterance to the TTS sink / voice pipeline
- Check backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/utterance_sink.py and the bot's audio bridge to the Meet room
- Check whether the bot's microphone in the Meet session is actually unmuted at the moment of speaking
- Cross-check with [[persist-bot-utterances-to-meeting-history-everything-the-bot-says]] (Johnny-awh) — once utterances are logged, we can see whether the approved text ever reached the TTS layer
- Related to [[review-and-standardize-bot-free-mode-speech-decision-logic]] (Johnny-vgl) — same underlying 'bot doesn't actually speak' family of symptoms, different trigger

## Acceptance

- User approves a pending suggestion
- Within ~2 seconds the approved text is heard in the Meet session
- The spoken utterance is logged in the meeting history (depends on Johnny-awh)

title: Pending approvals don't appear in UI until page is refreshed
description:
## What's broken

When the bot generates a suggestion that requires user approval, the pending approval does not appear in the UI in real time. The user has to manually refresh the page to see new pending approvals.

## Expected behavior

Pending approvals should appear automatically as soon as the bot routes a suggestion to the approval queue — within ~1 second, without any user action.

## Likely root cause

The UI is not subscribed to a real-time channel for approval events (no WebSocket / Server-Sent Events / polling). The approval queue is fetched once on page load and never refreshed.

## Acceptance

- Open the meeting/approval view
- Trigger the bot to generate a suggestion (e.g., speak something the router will defer for approval)
- New pending approval appears in the UI within ~1 second, no refresh needed
- Resolved approvals (approved/rejected) also update in real time
- Works across multiple browser tabs simultaneously

title: Persist bot utterances to meeting history (everything the bot says)
description:
## Why this exists

Currently the bot's transcriptions/utterances (everything it says into the meeting) are not consistently persisted to the meeting history. Without this, the user cannot review what the bot actually said after the meeting, audit autonomous-mode behavior, or debug why a suggestion did/did not get spoken.

The history must be the single source of truth for both:
- What participants said (already partially captured in transcript_chunks)
- What the bot said (currently missing or inconsistent)

## What needs to happen

- Every bot utterance — whether triggered by free mode, suggested-and-approved mode, autonomous mode, or any other path — must be persisted to the meeting history with:
  - session_id
  - timestamp
  - utterance text
  - source/mode that triggered it (suggestion-approved / autonomous / scripted / etc.)
  - linkage to the originating router decision or LLM response if applicable
- Existing sinks (see backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/transcript_sink.py and utterance_sink.py) should be reviewed to ensure they capture bot output, not only inbound STT
- UI: the meeting/session view must show bot utterances inline with participant transcripts so the timeline is complete
- Backfill: confirm historical sessions either get utterances backfilled where data exists or are clearly marked as incomplete

## Acceptance

- After a real Google Meet session, the history view shows every phrase the bot spoke, in order, distinguishable from participant transcript chunks
- Records survive container restart and are queryable in PostgreSQL
- Free-mode suggestions that were NOT spoken are also recorded (as suggestions) so the decision audit trail is complete

Related: [[review-and-standardize-bot-free-mode-speech-decision-logic]] (Johnny-vgl) — the free-mode decision logic must surface its outcome here.

title: Review and standardize bot free mode speech decision logic
description:
In free mode, the bot generates suggested responses (shown in UI like 'Suggested: ...') but does not actually speak them in the meeting. The decision-making process for when/whether the bot speaks is unclear and inconsistent.

This functionality needs to be reviewed and standardized:
- How is the decision made for the bot to speak vs. just suggest?
- What triggers actual speech output in free mode?
- How does free mode differ from other modes (guided, scripted, etc.)?
- Standardize the behavior so suggestions and actual speech are aligned with mode semantics

Context: Observed during a live meeting test where the bot showed a confident suggested response ('Yes I am! Nice to meet you all...') but never spoke it aloud in the Google Meet session.

title: Install piper-tts in api/worker (and meet-worker) image and mount piper_models volume
description: Same shape as Johnny-1gl but for the Piper TTS provider. The api container has no piper binary on PATH so the /providers/{id}/test smoke call fails. The meet-worker image also does not install piper despite SETUP_LOCAL.md claiming it ships pre-installed — fix both. Use the piper-tts PyPI wheel (provides the piper CLI). Also mount the piper_models named volume in api/worker so voice ONNX files downloaded by any service are visible everywhere.
close_reason: api/worker Dockerfile installs piper-tts via --extra local-tts; meet-worker Dockerfile pins piper-tts==1.4.2; api/worker compose services mount piper_models; verified POST /providers/172/test returns ok=true with 15604 bytes synthesized after downloading en_US-john-medium into the volume.

title: Install faster-whisper in api/worker image and mount whisper_models volume
description: The Test button in admin Providers UI calls POST /providers/{id}/test inside the api container, which runs a real transcribe_stream against the configured STT provider. For faster-whisper that requires the library to be importable in the api container; today only the meet-worker image ships it. Also api/worker need read access to the whisper_models named volume so cached CTranslate2 weights are shared with the meet-worker.
close_reason: api/worker Dockerfile now installs faster-whisper via uv sync --extra local-stt; api/worker compose services mount the whisper_models volume; verified by hitting POST /providers/136/test which returns ok=true after pre-warming the base model into the volume.

title: Verify ElevenLabs TTS provider works end-to-end with updated API key
description:
The ELEVENLABS_API_KEY value in .env has been replaced with a real ElevenLabs key (previously it contained a Google API key starting with AIzaSy... which caused HTTP 401 Invalid API key responses).

Now verify the ElevenLabs TTS adapter actually works end-to-end against the live ElevenLabs API:

1. Re-run `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` and confirm the tts-elevenlabs row PASSes (no more 401).
2. Hit `POST /providers/{id}/test` directly against the seeded elevenlabs provider row and confirm it returns success with synthesized audio bytes (non-empty payload, valid audio content-type).
3. Exercise the provider in a real meeting context: trigger an agent_utterance in auto_speak_limited mode and confirm the resulting audio is generated via ElevenLabs and surfaces in the meeting audio bridge.
4. Capture the voice ID / model used in the request and persist a short note in the provider config so the working values are reproducible.
5. Close this issue only after a real Meet session has played back an ElevenLabs-synthesized utterance audibly to the user account.
close_reason: ElevenLabs TTS confirmed working — no further verification needed

title: Execute comprehensive end-to-end validation: bot joins real Google Meet and exercises every product feature across all modes
description:
## Why this exists

The lived product journey: Johnny (bot account, nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi) joins a real Google Meet via the Test calendar event, and every feature exposed by the app is exercised against the live session. The user observes/drives the meeting from nikita.rabykin@gmail.com.

This is the **master functional validation** for the Johnny product:
- Johnny-f7k smoke-tests infrastructure (`.env`, services, models).
- Johnny-upg drives the provider management UI.
- Johnny-ckz Part B builds an automated harness command.
- **This task is the full coverage run** that proves the actual product (join → listen → decide → speak → audit) works against a real Google Meet, in every mode, with every UI surface verified.

## Testing identities (do not confuse)

- **Bot identity (Johnny in the app)**: `nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi`, role=bot
- **Observer / driver (Meet participant)**: `nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`
- **Test calendar event**: single event titled "Test", owner=`nikita.rabykin@gmail.com`, both accounts invited, Meet link attached, freely modifiable between runs

## When to run

- After Johnny-ckz Part A (join-stuck bug fix) lands — without it, every phase past Phase 3 will fail.
- Re-run whenever any of the following changes: join path (Playwright, Xvfb, PulseAudio, Google sign-in), audio bridge, Pipecat pipeline, VAD, router LLM, answer LLM, TTS, persistence layer (transcript_chunks / agent_decisions / agent_utterances), live session UI, history view, identity switching, scheduler.

## How to run

- **Preferred**: via Johnny-ckz Part B harness — `uv run python -m johnny.e2e --mode=<mode>` for each of the four modes — once it is built.
- **Fallback (works today)**: execute the phases below manually with chrome-devtools-mcp driving every UI verification and the observer account driving Meet audio.

Either path must produce the same evidence package (screenshots + JSON report under `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`) and the same PASS/FAIL roll-up.

## Scope: every product surface

- **Calendar surface**: fetch, refresh, select event, configure bot
- **Profile templates**: applied via meeting_config with overrides
- **Identity switching**: bot account vs user account
- **Scheduler**: detects upcoming meeting, spawns worker, stops on time
- **Meet worker**: Playwright joins, Xvfb + PulseAudio configured, mic muted / camera off by default
- **Audio bridge**: capture meeting audio, playback synthesized audio into virtual mic
- **Pipecat pipeline**: VAD → STT → router LLM → answer LLM → TTS
- **All four modes**: listen / suggest / approval / auto_speak_limited
- **Browser push notifications + in-UI approvals**
- **Persistence**: transcript_chunks, agent_decisions, agent_utterances
- **Live session UI**: transcript pane, decision feed, pending approvals
- **History view**: list, detail, pgvector transcript search, export, delete

## Out of scope

- Performance benchmarking and latency budgets
- Multi-tenant / multi-user fixtures (single Test event, single bot, single observer)
- Concurrent meetings / load tests
- CI integration (follow-up task)
- AWS / cloud deployment paths

title: End-to-end UI test of provider management via chrome-devtools-mcp
description:
## Why this exists

The user has populated `.env` with real API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs (cloud), plus Ollama (local LLM via OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The provider settings UI at `/providers` (US-018, Johnny-kgc.18) is the only path real users will use to add, test, switch, and remove providers — but right now no automation exercises that path. A regression in the form, the registry endpoint, the encryption pipeline, or the active-row selector would ship undetected because the existing tests cover the API in isolation, not the UI flow.

Johnny-f7k handles the backend `.env` smoke (cheap API probes against each provider key) but never touches the browser. This task closes the gap: drive the real SvelteKit UI with chrome-devtools-mcp, exercise every provider end-to-end, assert both UI state and database state at every step, and produce a PASS/SKIP/FAIL report plus screenshot artifacts.

## Goal

Build a re-runnable E2E harness that proves the provider management UI works for every supported backend against the keys already present in `.env`. The harness:

- Runs against a live Docker Compose stack
- Drives a real browser via chrome-devtools-mcp
- Adds, tests, sets-active, switches, and removes every provider for every kind (STT / LLM / TTS)
- Skips any provider whose `.env` key is blank (no false failures)
- Captures screenshots and a JSON report into `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`
- Exits non-zero on any FAIL so it can gate CI

## Scope: per-kind x per-provider matrix

**STT**
- Deepgram (cloud) — `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`
- OpenAI Realtime STT (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- FasterWhisper (local) — model file in `whisper_models` volume; SKIP if not present

**LLM**
- OpenAI (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- Anthropic (cloud) — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- Gemini (cloud) — `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY`
- OpenAI-compatible / Ollama (local) — `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` reachable; SKIP otherwise

**TTS**
- ElevenLabs (cloud) — `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`
- OpenAI TTS (cloud) — `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- Piper (local) — voice file in `piper_voices` volume; SKIP if not present

## Per-provider flow

For each provider with a configured key:

1. Navigate to `/providers`
2. Click "Add provider" for the right kind
3. Select the backend from the dropdown
4. Fill the form (credentials + config). The harness is **schema-aware**: it calls `GET /providers/schemas` if available (post-Johnny-mma) and renders field-by-field; otherwise it falls back to filling the current generic `Credentials` and `Options` textareas with the right `key=value` lines.
5. Submit
6. Assert row visible in the list with the expected name and kind
7. Assert row present in `GET /providers` API response
8. Click "Test" on the row
9. Assert test result rendered as success in UI within 10s
10. Assert success surfaced via `POST /providers/{id}/test` response code
11. Set the row as active for its kind
12. Assert active indicator visible in UI
13. Assert exactly one provider per kind has `is_active=true` in DB
14. Screenshot

After all providers of a kind are added:

15. Switch active between two providers of the same kind; assert UI and DB switch
16. Delete each provider one at a time
17. Assert row removed from UI and DB after each delete
18. Verify behavior when deleting the active provider — auto-promote another or require explicit unset, whichever matches the implemented contract

## Error and edge cases

- **Invalid API key** — fill with `sk-invalid-deadbeef`; Test button must report failure with HTTP status and readable UI error
- **Missing required field** — submit with a required field blank; form must reject with field-level error and make no API call
- **Duplicate name** — adding a second provider with the same `name` must be rejected with a clear UI message
- **Provider with no `.env` key** — SKIP gracefully with `reason` in the report, never FAIL
- **Network failure during Test** — `/providers/{id}/test` should surface a transient error and the UI must not get stuck in a loading state
- **Backend down mid-flow** — clean error toast, no UI crash

## chrome-devtools-mcp usage (REQUIRED — do NOT use claude-in-chrome)

Tools to load first via `ToolSearch`:

- `mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page` / `list_pages` / `select_page`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot` (accessibility tree — primary assertion handle)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot` (visual artifacts)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__fill` / `fill_form`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__click`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__wait_for`
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages` (capture browser errors)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests` (verify API traffic)
- `mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script` (last resort for state assertions)

Snapshot-based assertions (role + name) are preferred over XPath/CSS — they survive markup churn.

## Implementation

- Location: `tests/e2e/providers_ui/`
- Entrypoint: `uv run python -m tests.e2e.providers_ui` and `pytest -m e2e_ui` both work
- One Python module per kind: `test_stt.py`, `test_llm.py`, `test_tts.py`
- Shared fixtures: stack health check, schema fetcher, artifact directory factory, screenshot helper
- Final summary table (kind x backend x outcome) printed to stdout
- JSON report at `tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/report.json` for CI consumption
- Exit 0 only when no FAIL; SKIP does not block exit success
- Idempotent: harness deletes all provider rows at the start with a confirm prompt or `--force` for unattended runs
- Docs: `docs/E2E_TESTING.md` explains how to run, what is tested, and how to add a new provider

## Out of scope

- Provider performance benchmarking
- Cost tracking
- Long-form generation tests (verify connectivity, not depth)
- Mobile viewport testing
- A11y audit (separate task)
- Joining a real Meet — that is Johnny-ckz Part B
design:
- chrome-devtools-mcp ONLY (per CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/rules/common/browser-automation.md). Never claude-in-chrome.
- Schema-aware form filler: prefer `GET /providers/schemas`; fall back to the current generic Credentials/Options textareas if endpoint is 404. Lets the harness run today and survive Johnny-mma landing.
- DB assertions via `GET /providers` (and `GET /providers/{id}`) — never direct DB queries. Keeps the test honest about what the API exposes.
- Idempotent setup: harness deletes all provider rows at start with explicit `--force` for unattended runs. Avoids cross-run state bleed.
- Artifact dir per run (`tests/e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>/`) so historical comparison and CI upload are easy.
- Test isolation: each provider exercise is independent and tagged so `pytest -k` can run a single backend.
- Secrets handling: harness reads keys from `os.environ` only, never logs key values, and scrubs password-type fields from screenshots.

title: Smoke-test populated .env: bring stack up and verify end-to-end
description:
The user has populated .env with real keys (Google OAuth, Fernet, provider API keys). The setup guide (Johnny-mxx) and its bugfix (Johnny-i1d) made the documented commands runnable. The next concrete step is a repeatable smoke test that takes a populated .env and answers: "is this configuration actually usable, and where does it break?"

This task delivers a single command (or short script) the user can run after filling .env that verifies the whole stack stands up and the configured providers respond. It must produce a clear PASS/FAIL report per check so the user knows exactly what needs attention.

## What "smoke test" means here

The test is not a unit test — it is an integration probe that exercises real services with the real .env:

1. **Compose bring-up** — `docker compose up -d` succeeds, every service is healthy within a timeout (api, worker, frontend, postgres, redis).
2. **Migrations** — `alembic upgrade head` runs cleanly inside the api container against the live postgres.
3. **Fernet** — backend reads FERNET_KEY from env, encrypts and decrypts a sample value round-trip without error.
4. **Google OAuth config** — GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI are present and the consent URL builds without error (do not require a live user consent).
5. **Provider credentials sanity** — for each non-empty provider key in .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY), perform a 1-line cheap call (e.g. list models / list voices / `hi` completion of <= 5 tokens) and report the HTTP status. Skip providers whose keys are blank.
6. **Local model dirs** — JOHNNY_WHISPER_MODEL_DIR and JOHNNY_PIPER_MODEL_DIR resolve to writable mounts inside the meet-worker image; report whether expected model files are present and, if not, what to download.
7. **Ollama reachability** — if Ollama is the configured local LLM backend, hit `/api/tags` on the host and report the available models.
8. **Container launcher** — if JOHNNY_USE_DOCKER_LAUNCHER=true, verify the api/worker can talk to the Docker daemon and the meet-worker image is built/pulled.
9. **WebSocket** — `/ws/global` accepts a connection and immediately closes cleanly (no auth in MVP).
10. **Frontend** — `http://localhost:5173` returns 200 and the SvelteKit shell loads (chrome-devtools MCP screenshot for visual confirmation).

## How to deliver it

Pick one of these (whichever fits the codebase best — leave the choice to the implementer):

- A new make target / script: `scripts/smoke.sh` or `make smoke` that runs the checks and prints a colored PASS/FAIL table at the end.
- A backend CLI: `uv run python -m johnny.smoketest` that performs the in-process checks (Fernet, OAuth URL build, provider calls, model dirs) and shells out for the Compose/health checks.
- A pytest marker `@pytest.mark.smoke` plus `uv run pytest -m smoke` that uses the real .env (skip-if-blank for optional providers).

The chosen entrypoint should be documented in docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md as the very last step of "You finished — now verify".

## Output the user sees

The test must print one row per check with a status icon (PASS / SKIP / FAIL) and a one-line reason on failure. Example:

```
[PASS] docker compose services healthy (api, worker, frontend, postgres, redis)
[PASS] alembic upgrade head
[PASS] FERNET_KEY round-trip
[PASS] Google OAuth consent URL builds
[PASS] OPENAI_API_KEY        — models.list returned 200, 47 models
[SKIP] ANTHROPIC_API_KEY     — not set
[PASS] DEEPGRAM_API_KEY      — projects.list returned 200
[PASS] ELEVENLABS_API_KEY    — voices returned 200, 23 voices
[SKIP] GOOGLE_API_KEY        — not set
[PASS] Ollama reachable      — http://localhost:11434, 2 models (llama3.1, qwen2.5)
[PASS] Whisper models dir    — base.en present
[FAIL] Piper voices dir      — empty; download from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices
[PASS] Docker launcher       — meet-worker:latest image found
[PASS] WS /ws/global         — connect+close ok
[PASS] Frontend              — 200, shell rendered (screenshot: tmp/smoke/frontend.png)

12 PASS · 2 SKIP · 1 FAIL
```

Exit code is 0 if every non-SKIP check passed, 1 otherwise. SKIP is for optional providers with blank keys, never a failure.

## Out of scope
- Performing a real Google OAuth consent flow (would require a browser session and a real user).
- Joining a real Google Meet meeting end-to-end (that is a separate manual verification).
- Performance benchmarking (latency, throughput).
- Multi-account or LiveKit transport smoke (LiveKit-specific checks can be added once Johnny-kgc.25 is exercised in practice — for now JOHNNY_TRANSPORT=local is enough).
acceptance_criteria: A single documented entrypoint (script, make target, or pytest marker) runs the full smoke flow against a populated .env. The output prints one PASS/SKIP/FAIL row per check with a one-line reason on failure, and a final summary line. Skipped providers (blank keys) never cause a FAIL. Exit code is 0 only when every non-SKIP check passed. Checks include: docker compose healthy services, alembic upgrade, Fernet round-trip, Google OAuth URL build, per-provider live credential probes (cheap calls), Ollama reachability if configured, model directories, Docker launcher reachability if enabled, WebSocket connect, frontend HTTP 200 with screenshot. The smoke entrypoint is added as the final step of docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md. All quality gates pass: uv run pytest, uv run ruff check, uv run mypy, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint. Visual verification via chrome-devtools MCP captures the frontend shell.

title: Fix broken commands in docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md
description:
The setup guide created under Johnny-mxx has commands that fail for a fresh user:

1. python3 -c 'from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())' fails with ModuleNotFoundError because the user has no global cryptography install yet.
2. uv install is not a valid subcommand (uv uses 'uv sync' for installing project deps, or 'uv pip install' for ad-hoc installs).
3. The guide doesn't make clear when to install backend deps (uv sync) vs frontend deps (pnpm install) before doing other steps.

Fixes required:
- Replace the cryptography-based Fernet key generation with a stdlib-only one-liner: python3 -c 'import base64,secrets; print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(32)).decode())'
- Or use 'uv run --with cryptography python -c ...' so deps are auto-fetched
- Add a clear 'Install dependencies' step using 'uv sync' (backend) and 'pnpm install' (frontend) before any commands that require them
- Verify every copy-paste block in the guide actually works on a clean macOS/Linux machine
- Ensure ordering: clone -> install deps -> generate keys -> .env -> docker compose up

title: Bot carries the whole meeting's context (not a 6-turn rolling window) when routing and answering
description:
## Why this exists

Today the voice pipeline at \`backend/johnny/voice_pipeline/pipeline.py\` keeps the last **6** transcripts in memory and nothing else (\`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\`, line 69; rolling delete at line 850-851; window assembly at line 853-874). Older parts of the meeting fall out of the prompt entirely.

The static \`config.context\` field on a \`MeetingConfig\` exists (line 130, used at lines 740 and 789) but only carries pre-meeting context the user typed in by hand. Nothing accumulates *during* the meeting.

Effect: ten minutes into a meeting, the bot has forgotten the first nine minutes. Ask "what did we decide about the staging deploy earlier?" and it has no idea. That defeats most of the value of a long-form meeting bot.

## What "whole context" means here

Three layers, all needed:

1. **Pre-meeting context** — already there (\`config.context\`), but should also pull from the Google Calendar event's description / attachments / linked docs if available.
2. **In-meeting accumulation** — every finalised transcript from this session, in order, available to both router and answer LLMs, not capped at 6.
3. **Cross-session continuity (optional, smaller scope)** — if the same calendar event recurs (same recurring_event_id), surface the most recent prior session's summary as additional context. File a follow-up bead if too much; can be deferred.

## What to build

### Storage is already there

\`transcript_chunks\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py\` and the persistence layer in \`app/services/transcripts.py\`) already persists every finalised STT chunk per session — that's the source of truth. The pipeline just doesn't read from it; it works from its in-memory window.

### Pipeline changes

- Drop the \`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 6\` cap as the default. Replace with an unbounded list per session, capped by **token budget** instead of turn count.
- Make \`_build_input_window\` (line 853) emit the **full** session transcript when within budget, otherwise apply a rolling summarisation step: oldest N transcripts get collapsed into a short summary line ("Earlier: …"), recent transcripts kept verbatim.
- Token budget knobs configurable per provider (different LLMs have different windows). Default safe: 75 % of the provider's max context, reserving the rest for the answer.
- Summarisation can be a lightweight call to the same router/answer LLM with a "summarise the following meeting transcript in <= N sentences" prompt; cache the summary against the session so it's not recomputed every turn.

### Crash / resume

- On worker (re)start mid-session — e.g. container respawn — rehydrate \`_transcript_history\` from \`transcript_chunks WHERE session_id = ?\` so the bot doesn't reset to zero context.

### Calendar context

- Read the calendar event's \`description\` (already fetched per \`app/services/calendar_polling.py\`) and append it to the pipeline's system prompt as additional context, distinct from the user-typed \`config.context\` so both are visible to the LLM and persisted separately for audit.
- If the event has attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs in the description, **out of scope** for this bead — list as a follow-up.

### Persistence / audit

- The system prompt the LLM sees per turn (with full or summarised context) should be persisted on \`agent_decisions\` (or alongside it) so audits can reproduce why the bot answered the way it did. Today the snapshot in \`_build_input_window\` (line 858-873) captures \`transcript_window\` and \`instructions\` / \`context\` — extend with the summarised-history snapshot when summarisation kicks in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a 30+ minute session, asking the bot a question about something said in the first 5 minutes produces an answer that references that earlier context (not a "I don't know").
- [ ] No 6-turn cap on transcript history — capped by token budget instead.
- [ ] When over the token budget, oldest transcripts are summarised; the summary is cached per session and reused across turns.
- [ ] Pre-meeting context = \`config.context\` + calendar event description, both visible in the system prompt and persisted for audit.
- [ ] On worker container restart mid-session, the next turn picks up the full prior transcript from \`transcript_chunks\` (no context reset).
- [ ] The \`_build_input_window\` snapshot stored per decision includes whatever the LLM actually saw (full or summarised) so audits are reproducible.
- [ ] Token-budget knob is configurable per LLM provider; defaults to 75 % of the provider's max context.
- [ ] Tests cover: full session under budget, session over budget triggering summarisation, mid-session restart rehydration, calendar description merged into context.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Cross-session continuity for recurring events (file a follow-up under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it).
- Reading attached Google Docs / Sheets URLs from the event description (separate bead).
- Vector-search retrieval over transcripts (already a separate workstream — \`agent_decisions\` and \`transcript_chunks\` have embeddings via \`compute_pending_embeddings\`; this bead is about *in-session* context, not retrieval).
- Per-speaker memory / who-said-what diarisation upgrades.

## Notes

The current 6-turn cap was a scaffolding default, not a designed limit — \`config.transcript_window_size\` is already configurable. This bead is the natural next step: lift the cap, switch to token-budgeted, and persist what the LLM actually saw.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness). This bead reinforces the value the harness needs to prove.
- \`Johnny-ckz.2\` — Autonomous mode. Autonomous benefits most from full context since it has no per-utterance approval gate.
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation. When this lands, \`Johnny-pdf\` Phase 5/6/7 scripts should include a question that requires context from earlier in the same session, otherwise the test never exercises this.
- \`Johnny-kgc.33\` — US-033: Transcript and audit persistence. The data layer this bead reads from.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline no longer caps transcript history at 6 turns; carries the full session transcript within a configurable token budget, summarising older content when over budget; merges calendar event description into pre-meeting context; rehydrates from transcript_chunks on worker restart; persists whatever the LLM actually saw per decision; tests cover under-budget, over-budget, restart, calendar merge; quality gates pass.

title: Add 'Autonomous' mode: bot speaks freely per profile instructions, no whitelist, no approval gate
description:
## Why this exists

Today \`BotMode\` (\`backend/app/db/models.py:51-55\`) ships four values:

1. \`listen_only\` — STT only, bot never speaks.
2. \`suggest_only\` — pipeline runs, decisions logged, bot stays silent.
3. \`approval_required\` — pipeline proposes a reply, user must Approve/Reject in the UI before it speaks.
4. \`limited_auto_speak\` — bot speaks, but only verbatim from the profile template's \`allowed_replies\` whitelist (currently required for this mode at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\`).

There's no mode for "let Johnny act on its own, guided only by the profile template's instructions and context". The user wants exactly that: free-form generation, no approval round-trip, no allowed-reply whitelist — the bot self-governs against the profile instructions.

This is the natural fifth mode that the existing scaffolding was clearly designed to support but never delivered.

## What to build

### New enum value

- Add \`AUTONOMOUS = "autonomous"\` to \`BotMode\` in \`backend/app/db/models.py\`. Naming options considered: \`AUTO_SPEAK\` (parallel with \`LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\`), \`FREE_SPEAK\`, \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`UNRESTRICTED\`. Recommendation: \`AUTONOMOUS\` — communicates the *intent* (operates on its own per instructions) rather than the surface behaviour. UI label: "Autonomous".
- Alembic migration in \`backend/alembic/versions/\` extending the PG enum type. Pattern to follow: \`0003_decision_outcome_suggested.py\` already adds a value to an enum and is the template to copy.

### Validation rules

- \`allowed_replies\` requirement at \`app/api/templates.py:52\` and \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:138\` is currently \`if mode is BotMode.LIMITED_AUTO_SPEAK\` — leave it as-is. For \`AUTONOMOUS\`, \`allowed_replies\` must be **empty or ignored** (the whole point is no whitelist).
- Profile template instructions and context **must be non-empty** for \`AUTONOMOUS\` — they are the only governance. Add a parallel validation that rejects an autonomous-mode template/meeting_config with blank instructions.

### Pipeline behaviour

- Reuse the existing router → answer → TTS path (same as approval/limited_auto_speak).
- Skip the approval gate entirely (no \`agent_decisions.status = pending\`, no browser push, no countdown).
- No whitelist match against \`allowed_replies\` — the answer LLM's free-form output goes straight to TTS.
- Decisions are still persisted to \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome = spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` if the router declines, e.g. low confidence / non-question) so the audit trail stays intact.
- Honour the same per-session rate limit knobs the limited mode uses (cost + talking-over-others control), but default the cap a bit lower for autonomous since each utterance is free-form and longer. Make the cap overrideable per meeting_config.

### Frontend

- Add the new mode to \`frontend/src/lib/templates.ts\` — both the union type (line 10-13), the iteration list (16-19), and the human label map (23-26). Suggested label: \`'Autonomous'\`.
- Add the mode to \`frontend/src/lib/sessionDetail.ts\` (line 24-26 area) so the session detail view renders it.
- Surface a small "no approval, no whitelist — driven by profile instructions" note in the mode picker so a user picking Autonomous knows what's at stake.
- The template form should make \`instructions\` required when the mode is \`autonomous\` (mirror the backend validation).

### API

- Schemas at \`app/api/sessions.py:146\`, \`app/api/meeting_configs.py:65,89,128\`, \`app/api/templates.py:39,72\` already type as \`BotMode\` — they will accept the new value automatically once the enum lands, but verify with a unit test per endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] \`BotMode.AUTONOMOUS\` exists and is persisted via meeting_configs and templates.
- [ ] Alembic migration adds the value to the PG enum and \`alembic upgrade head\` is clean against a populated database.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config rejects blank \`instructions\` with a clear validation error.
- [ ] Autonomous-mode template / meeting_config does **not** require \`allowed_replies\`.
- [ ] In an autonomous session, the router proposes a reply, the answer LLM produces free-form output, TTS speaks it within ~4s of the question — no approval round-trip.
- [ ] Decisions still land in \`agent_decisions\` with \`outcome=spoken\` (or \`suppressed\` for declined cases); \`agent_utterances\` rows persist as in other speaking modes.
- [ ] Per-session rate limit applies; over-cap requests log a \`suppressed\` decision with \`reason=rate_limited\`.
- [ ] Frontend renders 'Autonomous' as a fifth option in the mode picker and on the session detail view.
- [ ] Quality gates pass: \`uv run pytest\`, \`uv run ruff check\`, \`uv run mypy\`, \`pnpm typecheck\`, \`pnpm lint\`.

## Out of scope

- Per-template instruction templates / prompt library.
- Anti-jailbreak guardrails against malicious instructions — the bead assumes the user owns their template.
- Voice-tone / persona tuning (uses whatever the configured TTS provider produces).
- A "kill switch" UI button to immediately silence an autonomous bot mid-meeting — file a follow-up bead under \`Johnny-ckz\` if you want it; it's a different shape of work.

## Notes

This belongs under \`Johnny-ckz\` because the lived-journey validation in \`Johnny-pdf\` (Phases 4-7 explicitly enumerate all four modes) needs a fifth phase or an extension of Phase 7 to cover Autonomous. When that lands, update \`Johnny-pdf\` acceptance to include the new mode.

## Related

- \`Johnny-ckz\` — parent epic (join-stuck fix + e2e harness).
- \`Johnny-pdf\` — master e2e validation, currently enumerates Phases 4-7 across the four existing modes; will need extending.
- \`Johnny-kgc.26\` — US-026: Listen-only and Suggest-only modes (closed; precedent for adding modes).
- \`Johnny-kgc.27\` — US-027: Approval-required mode (closed; reference for pipeline behaviour without approval gate).
- \`Johnny-kgc.28\` — US-028: Limited auto-speak (closed; nearest neighbour — same speak path, different governance).
acceptance_criteria: BotMode.AUTONOMOUS lands with migration; validation enforces non-empty instructions and ignores allowed_replies; pipeline speaks free-form output without an approval gate; decisions and utterances persist as in other speaking modes; per-session rate limit honoured; frontend exposes 'Autonomous' as the fifth mode option and on session detail; quality gates pass.
notes: Spawned 2026-06-06 from user request — explicitly wants a mode that lets the bot act on instructions alone with free speech and no per-utterance confirmation. Lives under Johnny-ckz so the e2e harness picks it up.

title: Surface undecryptable Google account tokens with a clear reconnect path
description:
When a stored Google account row's refresh token cannot be decrypted (typically because FERNET_KEY was rotated since the OAuth flow, or postgres data outlived the host .env), the Calendar page surfaces the raw backend error 'google api client error: failed to decrypt refresh token for account N' and offers no recovery path. The user is stuck at a dead end even though Settings → Disconnect can already clean the row up.

## Repro

1. Connect a Google account via /settings (account row stored, refresh token encrypted with key K1).
2. Regenerate FERNET_KEY (e.g. user re-ran the setup guide §3) and restart the stack — postgres volume persists.
3. Open /calendar — Refresh attempt against /calendar/events?account_id=N raises GoogleApiClientError → 502 → top-of-page red error.

## Root cause

backend/app/services/google_client.py:96-102 — _decrypt_refresh_token() raises GoogleApiClientError with the literal account id. backend/app/api/calendar.py:117-121 maps it to HTTP 502 with the bare exception string. The frontend (frontend/src/routes/calendar/+page.svelte:104-111) just renders error.message.

## Fix (proposed scope)

Backend:
- Introduce a distinct error class (e.g. TokenUndecryptableError) or carry a structured code on the existing GoogleApiClientError so callers can tell 'tokens unreadable, needs reauth' apart from transport / quota / scope errors.
- Map this code to a dedicated HTTP status (409 Conflict with detail {code: 'account_needs_reauth', account_id, email}) on /calendar/events and any other endpoint that calls GoogleApiClient (calendar polling worker should mark the row dirty and skip rather than throwing).
- Add a 'token_health' field to the AccountRead response: 'ok' | 'needs_reauth'. Computed cheaply at list time by attempting a no-op decrypt of refresh_token_encrypted (do not fetch userinfo).

Frontend:
- Settings: badge accounts whose token_health=='needs_reauth' as 'Token unreadable — reconnect'. Reuse the existing Add-account OAuth flow with the same role / default-user tags; on success, the row is replaced in place because upsert is keyed by email (google_client.py:265).
- Calendar: when the selected account.token_health=='needs_reauth', skip the /calendar/events call entirely and render an empty state with a deep link to /settings#account-N and a 'Reconnect this account' inline action that initiates OAuth right there.

Docs:
- docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 — move the 'if you lose the key, all encrypted rows must be deleted' warning to a callout at the top of the section. Add a copy-paste recovery snippet that disconnects all accounts via the API (which is already key-loss-safe per auth.py:474-479) instead of dropping postgres data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New typed error path distinguishes 'undecryptable token' from other GoogleApiClient failures
- [ ] /auth/google/accounts response includes token_health for every row, computed without a Google round-trip
- [ ] GET /calendar/events returns 409 with {code: 'account_needs_reauth'} (not 502) when the selected account's token cannot be decrypted
- [ ] Settings page shows a 'Reconnect' affordance for accounts in needs_reauth state; clicking it runs OAuth and the row is replaced after callback
- [ ] Calendar page detects needs_reauth before fetching and renders a non-error empty state with a Settings deep link
- [ ] Recovery callout added at the top of docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md §3 with the disconnect-via-Settings instruction
- [ ] Backend tests cover: undecryptable refresh token → typed error, /calendar/events 409 response, /auth/google/accounts token_health field
- [ ] Frontend tests cover: Settings reconnect button visibility, Calendar empty-state branch
- [ ] chrome-devtools screenshot of Calendar empty state and Settings reconnect badge attached

## Non-goals

- In-place key rotation (decrypt with old key, re-encrypt with new key) — out of scope; user is told to reconnect instead
- Multi-key support / key versioning on encrypted columns
- Detecting and auto-clearing meeting_configs whose identity_account is broken — Disconnect already cascades with force=true; document that path instead

## Notes

Current immediate workaround: /settings → Disconnect on the broken account (already handles undecryptable tokens — auth.py:474-479) → re-add via 'Add account'.

title: Refactor provider settings UI: per-provider structured forms instead of generic Credentials/Options textareas
description:
The current provider settings UI (US-018, Johnny-kgc.18) exposes only two generic textareas per provider — "Credentials" and "Options" — both accepting raw key=value lines. This is opaque: users must already know the exact env-var-style keys each provider expects (e.g. DEEPGRAM_API_KEY vs api_key vs token; OLLAMA base_url vs OPENAI_API_BASE; ElevenLabs voice_id vs voice). It causes silent typos, hides which fields are required, and makes provider switching painful.

This task replaces the two-textarea design with structured, row-based forms — one form schema per concrete provider adapter. Each provider type renders its own clearly labeled fields with inline guidance (placeholders, descriptions, links to where to get the value), required/optional markers, validation, and field grouping (auth vs config vs model selection).

The backend provider registry (US-011) already knows each provider's required/optional fields; this task surfaces that schema to the frontend rather than dumping a free-text textarea on the user.

## Scope

### Backend
- Extend the provider adapter base classes (STTProvider, LLMProvider, TTSProvider) with a class-level `field_schema()` classmethod that returns a list of field definitions: { name, label, type (text/password/url/number/select), required, placeholder, help_text, default, options? (for select), group? }
- Each concrete adapter (DeepgramSTT, OpenAIRealtimeSTT, FasterWhisperSTT, OpenAI LLM, Anthropic LLM, Gemini LLM, OpenAICompatibleLLM, ElevenLabsTTS, OpenAITTS, PiperTTS) declares its own field_schema with the right fields, labels, and help text
- New endpoint GET /providers/schemas returns all registered provider schemas grouped by kind so the frontend can render dynamic forms
- Persist values into the existing provider_credentials table — split fields into "credentials" (encrypted) and "config" (plain) buckets server-side based on the schema's type/sensitivity
- Validation: backend validates incoming payloads against the schema (required, type) before save; returns 422 with field-level errors
- Migration is not required if the underlying storage already uses JSONB; this is a UI/schema-presentation refactor, not a data-model rewrite

### Frontend
- New `/providers` UI replaces the two textareas with a per-provider form generated from the schema fetched from /providers/schemas
- Each provider card shows: provider name, kind badge, set of structured rows (label + input + help text + required marker), Test button, Save button, Delete button
- Field types render appropriately: password fields are masked, select fields use a dropdown, URL fields show a leading protocol hint, etc.
- Inline help text links to the provider's signup/docs page when relevant ("Get a key →")
- Validation surfaces both client-side (required, type) and server-side (422 field errors)
- The previous free-text textareas are removed entirely — no fallback raw mode

## Why this matters now
- The interactive wizard (Johnny-61y) will reuse the same schema source of truth, so a structured field_schema benefits both UI and CLI
- The setup guide (Johnny-mxx) can reference exact field names from the schema instead of pseudo-keys
acceptance_criteria: Backend: each provider adapter declares field_schema(); GET /providers/schemas returns schemas grouped by kind; payload validation returns field-level 422 errors. Frontend: /providers page renders a structured form per provider with labeled rows, help text, password masking, select dropdowns, URL hints, and required markers — no generic key=value textareas remain. Test button still works against the structured form. Setup wizard (Johnny-61y) consumes the same field_schema source of truth. All quality gates pass: uv run pytest, uv run ruff check, uv run mypy, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint. Visual verification via chrome-devtools MCP with screenshots of at least one cloud and one local provider form.

title: Build interactive CLI setup wizard for Johnny
description:
Build a Python CLI wizard that walks the user through Johnny's full local setup interactively. The wizard should be the friendlier alternative to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md — instead of copy-pasting commands, the user answers prompts and the wizard does the work.

The wizard should:

- Run via 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' or a script entrypoint like 'johnny setup'
- Use a rich TUI library (questionary, rich, or textual — pick one and stick to it)
- Detect prerequisites (Docker, uv, pnpm, available disk space, GPU presence) and report what is missing with direct install links
- Guide Google OAuth setup: open the Google Cloud Console URL in the default browser, prompt for client ID / client secret, write to .env
- For each provider kind (STT, LLM, TTS), ask: cloud or local?
  - If cloud: list options (Deepgram, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, ElevenLabs) with provider sign-up URLs and 'best for' notes; prompt for API key; write to .env and call backend API to register
  - If local: list recommended models per kind with size on disk and quality notes; let user pick; download automatically via huggingface-hub, ollama pull, or direct URL; place in correct volume path; call backend API to register
- Recommend best defaults per kind for local-first (e.g., faster-whisper small for STT, Llama 3.1 8B via Ollama for LLM, Piper en_US-amy-medium for TTS)
- Generate FERNET_KEY automatically and write to .env (only if missing)
- After provider setup, run the same smoke test the Providers UI offers ('Test' button) for each registered provider and report pass/fail
- Offer to start the Docker Compose stack at the end and open the UI
- Be re-runnable safely: detect already-completed steps and offer to skip or reconfigure
- Provide a '--non-interactive' mode that reads answers from a YAML file for CI / scripted setups

The wizard is a complement to docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md (Johnny-mxx), not a replacement — the docs should reference it as the recommended path.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard runs via a single 'uv run python -m johnny.wizard' command; detects missing prerequisites with install links; configures Google OAuth, all three provider kinds (cloud and local), and FERNET_KEY end-to-end; downloads local models automatically into the correct Docker volumes; runs provider smoke tests and reports pass/fail; safely re-runnable; supports --non-interactive YAML mode

title: Write local-first setup guide with copy-paste commands and direct download links
description:
Create a step-by-step setup guide for running Johnny entirely locally. The guide must be copy-paste ready, super simple, and include direct download links for every model and dependency.

The guide should cover:
- Prerequisites (Docker, uv, pnpm, Python version, disk space requirements)
- Cloning the repo and running 'docker compose up'
- Creating the dedicated johnny-bot Google account and registering OAuth desktop client (direct links to Google Cloud Console pages)
- Filling .env with all required variables (FERNET_KEY generation command, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)
- Local STT setup: which faster-whisper model size to pick (recommendation + size on disk), exact HuggingFace URL, where to place the file, config entry
- Local LLM setup: recommended model (e.g., Qwen2.5 7B or Llama 3.1 8B), Ollama vs vLLM choice, exact 'ollama pull' command or vLLM Docker command, base_url to put in provider config

- First-run smoke test: connect Google account, mark a test meeting, verify bot joins
- Troubleshooting section: PulseAudio not found, model file missing, OAuth redirect failure, container OOM

The output should be a single markdown file at docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md. Every command must be copy-pasteable. Every download must be a direct link. Assume the reader knows Docker basics but nothing about the AI stack.

description:

title: Johnny — Google Meet AI Meeting Bot
description:
Johnny is a single-user AI assistant that joins Google Meet meetings on the user's behalf and can listen, transcribe, suggest replies, ask for approval, or speak autonomously within configured constraints.

title: Read Google Docs/Sheets URLs linked in calendar event description and include as pre-meeting context
description:
**Why this exists**

Johnny-ckz.3 plumbed the calendar event description into the bot's system prompt as pre-meeting context. Users frequently paste Google Docs / Sheets / Drive links into the event description as the meeting agenda or background reading. Today those URLs reach the bot as plain text — the bot sees the link but can't read the document.

**What to build**

When the calendar event description contains links to Google Docs / Sheets / Drive files, fetch their contents (with the meeting identity's OAuth token), extract the text body, and append to the pipeline's calendar_context distinct from the URL list itself.

Implementation sketch:
- Add 'app/services/calendar_link_resolver.py' that detects 'docs.google.com/document/d/.*' and 'docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/.*' patterns in description text.
- For each, use the Google Drive / Docs / Sheets API (via existing GoogleApiClient) to fetch text content.
- Concatenate into 'calendar_attachments_text' on LaunchContext / PipelineConfig.
- Cap total fetched text by a reasonable size (e.g. 20k chars) so we don't blow the pipeline's token budget.
- Cache fetched content per (event_id, etag) so a polling cycle doesn't re-fetch unchanged docs.

**Out of scope**

- Slack / Notion / generic URL fetching (separate auth surface).
- Image / chart extraction from the docs (text only).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Calendar event description with a Google Docs link → the doc's text body lands in the bot's system prompt.
- Sheets link → tabular contents lands.
- Sheets with multiple tabs → handled.
- Drive permission denied → logged + the link continues to ride as plain text (no crash).
- Fetched content cached + invalidated on Drive etag change.

**Related**

- Johnny-ckz.3 — parent that added the description column.

title: Cross-session continuity: rehydrate prior session summary for recurring events
description:
**Why this exists**

The bead explicitly deferred *cross-session* continuity: when a user runs the same recurring meeting next week, the bot starts the new session with no memory of what was decided last time.

**What to build**

When a new bot_session is created for a calendar_event whose 'recurring_event_id' matches a previous bot_session, pull the most recent prior session's transcript summary and inject it as an additional context layer (distinct from `config.context` / `config.calendar_context` so the audit row can tell them apart).

Implementation sketch:
- Add 'session_summary' column to 'bot_sessions' (or a new 'session_summaries' table keyed by bot_session_id) populated at session close.
- New helper in 'app/services/history.py' to look up the prior session for a recurring event.
- New 'PipelineConfig.prior_session_context' field rendered in both router and answer LLM system prompts as 'Last session summary: <text>'.
- Pipeline_runner reads via new env var 'JOHNNY_PRIOR_SESSION_CONTEXT'.

**Out of scope**

- Multi-session retrieval (vector search across all prior sessions — separate workstream).
- Surfacing prior session summary in the UI (the bead is about pipeline context, not display).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Pipeline emits a prior-session-summary line in the system prompt when a recurring event has past sessions.

title: TTS providers: play a demo phrase after Test so the user actually hears the voice
description:
## Why this exists

The provider page at \`/providers\` already has a **Test** button per provider. For TTS providers the test currently synthesizes the word \`"hi"\`, counts the bytes, and discards them — see \`backend/app/api/providers.py:520\` (\`async for frame in instance.synthesize_stream("hi")\`). The UI only shows "Test OK" / "Test failed". The user has no way to *hear* what the configured voice actually sounds like before wiring it into a real meeting.

That's the gap. A working TTS provider with a wrong voice (mumbly, robotic, wrong language, wrong gender) is worse than a broken one because it slips into a real Meet and embarrasses you. Hearing a short demo phrase right at the moment of testing is the cheapest validation.

## What to build

Right after the existing Test button on \`/providers\` (and only for TTS providers — STT and LLM providers don't apply), play a short audio sample synthesized by that provider, in the browser, with a tiny inline player.

### Backend

- Either extend \`POST /providers/{id}/test\` so when \`kind=tts\` the response includes the synthesized audio (base64 + mime type + sample-rate hint), or add a sibling endpoint \`POST /providers/{id}/sample\` that returns \`audio/wav\` (or \`audio/mpeg\`) as the body. Sibling endpoint is the cleaner contract since the existing test response is JSON-shaped.
- Use a fixed, human-friendly demo phrase, not \`"hi"\`. Suggested: \`"Hi, this is Johnny. I can join your meeting and take notes."\` Keep it short (<= 25 words) so synthesis is cheap.
- Reuse the same provider instance lookup the \`/test\` endpoint uses; reuse \`provider.synthesize_stream(phrase)\` and concatenate frames into a single byte buffer.
- Wrap PCM frames into a WAV container (header + raw PCM) before returning so the browser can play it without any decoder hint — most TTS adapters yield raw PCM, not a complete container.
- Respect the provider's declared sample rate / channels when writing the WAV header.

### Frontend

- In \`frontend/src/routes/providers/+page.svelte\` near \`onTest\` (line 263) and the Test button (line 408): for TTS rows, on a successful test, also fetch the sample audio and play it through an \`<audio>\` element auto-created in the row's result area.
- Show a small "Play sample" button next to the "Test OK" line so the user can replay without re-running the synthesis.
- Disable / hide the player for STT and LLM kinds — keep the existing flow untouched there.
- Surface synthesis failures separately from the test pass/fail so the user can distinguish "test passed, voice unavailable for sample" from "test failed".

### Notes

- Browser autoplay policies: a user gesture (the Test click) is the trigger, so autoplay should be allowed. Add a defensive \`.catch()\` on \`audio.play()\` that surfaces a "Click to play sample" fallback button.
